title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-throughput-guarantees-util-reporting
author: Ava Park
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets were experiencing unfair burst consumption and capacity thrashing during short spikes, which caused customer-visible latency increases and misreported utilization. This PR implements a coordinated set of changes to the dedicated autoscaler and fleet runtime to provide explicit per-fleet throughput guarantees, improved burst token-bucket semantics, and richer utilization reporting for capacity planning. In short, this change: 1) introduces a configurable min_throughput_per_fleet setting that the autoscaler respects when scaling down so that critical fleets maintain a throughput floor, 2) refactors the burst tokenbucket allocator to use a per-fleet refill window and weighted distribution to avoid starvation when multiple routes spike concurrently, 3) adds a new autoscaler policy mode "throughput_guarantee" that can be toggled per-fleet and exposed in the Dedicated UI and API, 4) surfaces additional Prometheus metrics (fleet_min_throughput, burst_tokens_granted, burst_tokens_denied, scaledown_suppress_duration) and dashboard panels for utilization and burst denial rates, and 5) adds integration and e2e tests to validate behavior under synthetic spike workloads. Implementation notes: the autoscaler core now considers two new signals when computing desired replicas: effective_throughput (recent sustained tokens/sec) and burst_headroom (available burst tokens). When throughput_guarantee is enabled the desired replicas will not scale below ceil(min_throughput_per_fleet / per_replica_capacity) for the targeted fleet. The token-bucket allocator was moved into a dedicated coordinator service to make decisions across node pools and prevent double-allocation; this coordinator exposes a small gRPC API consumed by the serving runtime. Observability: metrics were added to the existing telemetry exporter and Redwood Console panels were updated to include a per-fleet burst denial line and an annotated scaledown_suppress chart. Testing: unit tests for allocator logic, new autoscaler unit tests, an integration test simulating 10s bursts across 8 routes, and an e2e scenario using the perf-canary harness were added. Rollout plan: feature gated behind autoscaler.policy=throughput_guarantee (off by default), staged rollout to Canary fleets for 48h, then to regions based on success criteria (<=5% increase in tail latency, >=20% decrease in burst denial incidents). Backwards compatibility: all existing autoscaler modes remain unchanged unless throughput_guarantee is enabled. See release_notes for user-facing changes.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice end-to-end design. Two asks: 1) can we add a metric that counts suppressed scaledowns so SRE can alert, and 2) validate coordinator gRPC is resilient to transient failures?

Ava Park (author): Added scaledown_suppress_duration metric and counter suppressed_scaledowns_count; coordinator gRPC has retry+backoff and a new circuit breaker with 5s cooldown (see coordinator/server.go).
Rina Kaur: Please check lock contention in allocator.go; I observed a potential hotspot when processing high concurrent bursts. Suggest using sharded mutexes or lock-free counters.

Ava Park (author): Refactored allocator to use sharded token buckets keyed by route hash and replaced a global mutex with per-shard locks; microbenchmark attached to the PR shows a ~3.6x throughput improvement under synthetic load.
Liam O'Neill: Tests look good. One nits: update API changelog about new autoscaler.policy values and add a migration note for infra teams.
Ava Park (author): Added docs/dedicated/release_notes.md and noted rollout steps/migration impact for infra teams.

release_notes: Added autoscaler policy 'throughput_guarantee' for Dedicated fleets; new config min_throughput_per_fleet; improved burst token-bucket allocator with weighted per-fleet refill to reduce burst denial; new observability metrics (burst_tokens_granted, burst_tokens_denied, suppressed_scaledowns_count, scaledown_suppress_duration) and Console panels; feature is feature-gated and off by default; rollout plan included in docs/dedicated/release_notes.md
